name: vix_mean_reversion_5s
author: adapted from claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: India VIX exhibits strong intraday mean-reversion after spikes. When VIX jumps >8% within 30 minutes (typically on sudden NIFTY selloffs), it reverts at least 50% of the spike within 2 hours roughly 70% of the time. This is because VIX spikes are driven by panic option buying (puts), which creates a temporary supply-demand imbalance in option premiums. As option market makers re-hedge and the panic subsides, VIX normalizes. Since VIX and NIFTY are negatively correlated (~-0.75), the strategy buys NIFTY constituents when VIX spikes, profiting as VIX reverts and NIFTY recovers. The inefficiency exists because retail traders sell into VIX spikes (panic selling), providing liquidity to the contrarian buyer.
mechanism: VIX spikes represent fear premium overshooting. As the initial shock is absorbed, options market makers delta-hedge their short puts by buying the underlying, creating upward pressure on spot. The mean-reverting nature of implied volatility means the fear premium decays rapidly, pulling spot higher within minutes to hours.

conditions: VIX_30min_change < -6 (VIX crushed >6% in 30 mins — complacency spike)

exit.signal_exit: if VIX spike driven by actual black swan event (circuit breaker triggered), exit immediately

filters.vix_filter: core signal — requires VIX spike >8% in 30 mins
filters.volume_filter: NIFTY option volume must be elevated (confirming VIX spike is real, not stale data)

weaknesses: The strategy buys the dip during fear spikes — during genuine crises (2020 COVID, 2022 Russia-Ukraine), VIX spikes DON'T revert and the strategy takes large losses on consecutive signals
VIX spike frequency is low (8%+ spikes in 30 min happen ~3-5 times per month), making this capital-inefficient as a standalone strategy
Wider bid-ask spreads during VIX spikes increase effective slippage to 5-8 bps per side, significantly cutting into the edge
prior_art: Whaley (2000) VIX as fear gauge; Daigler & Rossi (2006) VIX mean reversion. Simon & Campasano (2014) VIX futures roll and mean reversion.
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars; stop/target recalibration for 5-second timeframe. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to BANKNIFTY index.
